title: DFGNN: Dual-frequency Graph Neural Network for Sign-aware Feedback

problem.claim: Graph-based recommendation must model both positive and negative user feedback.

gap.claim: Using negative feedback in graph-based recommendation remains underexplored.

contributions.claim: The study reports that existing graph neural networks are not well-suited to modeling negative feedback as a high-frequency signal.
DFGNN models positive and negative feedback through a dual-frequency graph filter that captures low- and high-frequency signals.
Signed graph regularization maintains user and item embeddings uniformly in the embedding space to alleviate representation degeneration.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe DFGNN as a novel model for modeling positive and negative feedback from a frequency-filter perspective.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that existing graph neural networks are not well-suited for modeling negative feedback.
The authors report that graph-based recommendation suffers from representation degeneration.
The authors report extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrating the effectiveness of DFGNN.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph-based recommendation has achieved substantial success.
Existing approaches mainly model positive feedback while overlooking negative feedback.
The study identifies limitations in modeling negative feedback and a representation degeneration problem.
DFGNN uses dual-frequency filtering and signed graph regularization to address these limitations.
The authors report effectiveness based on experiments on real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: Positive and negative feedback are represented as low- and high-frequency signals.

interpretation.claim: Feedback with different graph-frequency characteristics may require distinct representation mechanisms.

application.claim: When modeling signed relational data, consider frequency-aware components that separately capture contrasting signal types.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this frequency interpretation applies beyond the reported recommendation setting.

source_observation.claim: Signed graph regularization is used to alleviate representation degeneration.

interpretation.claim: Embedding-space regularization can be paired with signal modeling to address both representation quality and feedback modeling.

application.claim: For signed graph models, evaluate whether embedding regularization reduces degeneration while preserving signal distinctions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the regularization objective, tuning requirements, or trade-offs.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide dataset names, sizes, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the experimental protocol or ablation results.
The abstract does not establish whether the code was released.
